checks.detail: Pass. The exact candidate launches res://main.tscn through the registered Godot runtime, reaches player control, renders a non-black 1280x720 scene, and reports no editor or runtime errors or missing resources.

Pass. Ordinary logical key and mouse-look input changed the player from (0.0,0.902,-0.006) to (0.569,1.992,-4.934), changed yaw to -22.69 degrees and pitch to 7.56 degrees, and preserved captured mouse input and the 76-degree camera contract.

Pass. The cumulative candidate retains the previously accepted runnable shell, deterministic player owner and ordinary input path; later authored-map and weapon additions do not invalidate the bootstrap technical baseline.

Pass. Fresh runtime state reports the accepted fixed spawn, collision-backed ground, authored daylight environment and Alpha at (-5,1.2,-23.2); ordinary traversal input changed the validated player and route-probe positions without fall-through or exposure failure.

Pass. Runtime reports exactly one authoritative Standoff environment instance with 11 visible meshes, 11 material slots, 30,379 collision triangles, ready navigation and clean validation of 14 visible meshes with no winding, tangent, NaN or dropped-triangle defects.

Pass. The accepted authored environment, outer datum, collision, navigation, human-scale camera and spawn-to-Alpha bindings remain coherent after the weapon integration; no duplicate or replacement map surface was observed.

Pass. White-box bindings preserve WASD, sprint, crouch, jump, logical mouse look, physical-F6 restart and R-only reload ownership. Fresh movement input exercised walk, sprint, crouch, jump, look and strafe; runtime position, velocity, yaw, pitch and route telemetry changed consistently while the authored world and camera exposure remained stable.

Pass. The complete receipt-backed component is directly instanced under Camera3D with both original profiles, coupled gun/hand assets, audio and effects. Fresh runtime inspection found the active 85-bone AK skeleton and intact weapon/hand bones, mesh validation was clean, and ordinary input produced a visibly different complete Saiga-12 rig. Matched frames show grounded two-hand weapon silhouettes, forward muzzles and clear central sight lines at 1280x720. The directional PRD reference alignment is concrete in the lower-right weapon/hands framing and daylight eye-level composition.

Fail. Ordinary fire, ADS, reload, switching and per-weapon ammo authority now exist, and fresh AK/Saiga hits each produced one shot ID, one ammo deduction and one target damage commit. However, the controlled-target hit branch has no world-space impact response: _resolve_ballistics calls _spawn_impact only for non-damageable blocked collisions, while controlled_target.gd only mutates health. Therefore a required hit does not drive muzzle/impact feedback exactly once from the authoritative shot event.

Fail. The authored map, locomotion and both coupled viewmodels are preserved and the core weapon authority is substantially implemented, but the integrated foundation cannot pass while controlled hits omit the required world-space impact observer from the authoritative shot chain.

required_criteria.requirement: Launch a minimal native Godot prototype with a simple bounded placeholder room, a player camera and ordinary keyboard/mouse input. This is an intentionally rough first increment: do not import the authored FPS map, real weapon or hand assets, HUD package, minimap package, enemy package or decorative asset collection. Verify the game starts without a black screen, missing-resource error or direct dependency on final content.

Use ordinary input to look and move the placeholder player inside the bounded prototype. Require stable camera framing, a visible floor, predictable input capture/release and a deterministic restart state. Placeholder geometry is permitted and expected; production scale, authored landmarks, weapons, HUD and map quality are explicitly out of scope.

Issue one narrow bootstrap verdict for the launchable placeholder loop. Accept only a real runnable shell and basic camera/input evidence; do not expand this first phase into map import, weapon implementation, HUD, minimap, enemy AI or final presentation.

Replace the accepted placeholder blockout with exactly one complete authored FPS environment from the asset pool. Launch through ordinary input and traverse its spawn-to-Alpha route. Require the PRD's 30-45 second effective spawn-to-A route budget with meaningful native cover and route decisions; reject moving Alpha close to spawn, shortening the route to make collision validation pass, or reporting a below-target route as acceptable. Require human-scale collision-backed ground, a fixed safe spawn, readable cover and landmarks, neutral daylight exposure, and no roof spawn, void, fall-through, decorative barriers, loose model placement or modular kit scatter. The authored map is first allowed in this phase; do not add real weapon/hand components, HUD, minimap or enemy AI yet.

Inspect the imported environment's complete native hierarchy, bounds, materials, collision and route datum. Require one intact instance supplying the dominant visible world, with product-owned outer support only. Reject extracted child meshes, broad proxy floors, cloned facades, missing textures, floating anchors, disconnected streets, raw-AABB minimap assumptions and source mutation.

Issue one map-integration verdict for the playable authored spawn-to-Alpha environment. The complete map, ground contact, collision, scale and route must be coherent in one ordinary-input run, and the route must preserve the PRD's 30-45 second effective travel budget rather than relocating Alpha to a trivial near-spawn endpoint. Do not require later weapon, HUD, minimap, enemy AI or cinematic behavior in this phase.

Use ordinary keyboard and mouse input to walk, strafe, sprint, crouch, jump and look across the accepted authored spawn-to-Alpha route. Preserve human scale, stable ground contact, collision-safe movement, readable camera height and FOV, and no shimmer, missing surfaces or exposure changes caused by camera movement.

Integrate the supplied AK-74M and Saiga-12 first-person components with their real hands/arms and animation rigs. Require plausible human scale, correct forward axis, two-hand contact, stable camera-relative framing, muzzle and optic alignment, weapon switching, ADS and reload visibility without clipping. Do not replace an intact component with a weaker reconstruction.

Through ordinary input, demonstrate AK-74M single and automatic fire, Saiga-12 fire, weapon switch, ADS, tactical/empty reload, dry fire, blocked shot, miss and controlled target hit. One authoritative shot event must drive ammo, recoil, animation, muzzle/impact feedback and audio exactly once. Do not build HUD, minimap or enemy AI yet; minimal world-space feedback is sufficient.

Issue one integrated weapon-foundation verdict for the accepted map and real weapon/hand components. Preserve the map and movement while proving the player-to-weapon causal chain. HUD skinning, minimap, enemy AI and final UI remain later work.
